additional_info.subject: Incident Report – Charging Irregularity on Sicharge D Station R6 313033014001 (22/07/2025)
additional_info.body:
Hello,
Please create a ticket for a detailed technical analysis regarding an incident on charging station Sicharge D – R6 313033014001.
Incident context:
•     Charging started: 22/07/2025 at 18:48:05
•     Charging ended: 22/07/2025 at 22:34:18
•     Vehicle connection: From 18:47:19 to 22:34:20
A driver reported abnormal behavior from the station:
“Last night, before going to bed, I noticed via the app that the truck wasn’t charging. I went back at 10:30 p.m. to restart the charge, which seemed to start correctly.
I had plugged it in at 6:45 p.m. with 33% battery, and it was stuck at 38%. The station showed ‘charging in progress’, but there was no power reading in kW. Did you get any alerts on your side? Definitely something to monitor.”
Extract from the log message:
•     Final SoC: 38%
•     Energy delivered: 26.13 Wh
•     Stop reason: EVDisconnected
•     Server timestamp: 22/07/2025
•     Transaction ID: 20874496
Request:
Please carry out a thorough technical analysis to identify the possible causes of this issue (no charging power despite “in progress” status, SoC stuck, etc.) and suggest corrective actions if needed.
I remain available for any further information.
Best regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0439554-DC/Si-D/FR-[Y2 / R6 313033014001]Charging Irregularity CRM:02681000525
additional_info.body:
Dear Malek DRIF,
We have analyzed the logs for the provided timestamp and observed repeated interruptions in the charging sessions. These interruptions were caused by the
"SuspendedEV" error
, indicating that the charging process was starting and stopping repeatedly.
Further investigation suggests a possible issue with the converter. We also noticed that the charger is currently running on an older firmware version.
As a first step, we recommend performing a
firmware update
to address this issue. If the problem persists after the update, we will plan for an on-site intervention to further diagnose and resolve the issue.
Kindly provide your permission to proceed with the firmware update at your earliest convenience.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Ankita

additional_info.body:
Dear Colleagues,
indly plan a site intervention to inspect the power converters of outlet  1. Please ensure a thorough check of all associated wirings and perform the following troubleshooting steps:
Troubleshooting Steps:
Check for any loose connections to all the power converters.
Use a multimeter to verify that the input voltage to each power converter is within the permissible range.
Identify the missing converter(s) using their serial numbers and confirm if they are powered on.
If any converter is missing or not powering on, please swap it with a known working unit and verify if it powers on.
Examine the power converter display for any error messages or indicator lights.
If all the above steps have been performed and the power converter still does not power on, please proceed with replacing it.
MLFB No.
